result.title: Learning Multimodal Sensor Fusion with JEPA Representations for Breathing Activity and Pose Recognition
result.comment: 6 pages, 2 figures, 3 equations, 4 tables, conference paper
result.summary: Predictive video representations do not by themselves specify how a multimodal system should handle missing sensors. We transfer frozen V-JEPA2 features to a set of heterogeneous sensors comprised by RGB video, depth video, and radar time series. A shared fusion model uses modality queries, fixed sensor slots, and explicit availability to classify breathing activity and pose from all seven non-empty sensor subsets. The contribution is a controlled evaluation of subset supervision, pooling capacity, and representation transfer on 39 OMuSense-23 subjects with five subject-group folds and three seeds. With matched downstream parameter counts, the final model reaches recording-level activity macro-F1 of $75.23%\pm0.60$ averaged across seven subsets. Supervising all subsets in each batch improves the matched query-pooling control by 1.923 percentage points (conditional 95% subject-bootstrap interval [0.647, 3.209]), while query pooling shows no clear advantage over matched mean pooling under balanced supervision. Radar probes support transfer beyond pooled wavelet pixels, 64-token inference approximately preserves mean activity performance, and the tested Consensus-JEPA loss adds no measured benefit against its exact control.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把冻结的 V-JEPA2 视频表征迁移到 RGB、深度与雷达等异构传感器，用带模态查询、固定传感器槽位和显式可用性的共享融合模型，在七种非空传感器子集上做呼吸活动与姿态分类，并以受控实验评估子集监督、池化容量与表征迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 「64 token 推理近似保持性能」以及固定槽位加显式可用性的设计，可能为 LVR 中的视觉 token 预算、证据筛选与缺失视觉证据处理提供可核查线索，但其任务是分类而非推理，迁移属推测。
